skill.name: coverage-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes Python test coverage reports, identifies uncovered critical paths, and recommends focused tests for improving coverage.
skill.summary: Find coverage gaps and plan targeted tests for Python projects.
skill.author: Atyantik

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, or sample snippets. One command substitution example is a legitimate coverage-history workflow but still runs nested shell commands and writes to a local file. A separate medium semantic finding notes that the skill suggests installing diff-cover without an explicit approval or isolation step.

remediation.issue: Shell command substitution in coverage history example
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user approval before running shell pipelines that write files, or split the workflow into visible steps.
Require user confirmation before running pip install diff-cover and recommend using an isolated project environment.

remediation.issue: Many command examples are presented without execution boundaries
remediation.suggestion: State that make, coverage, open, and pip commands are examples that should only run in trusted repositories.

content.value_statement: Low test coverage hides critical gaps and slows release decisions. This skill reviews coverage reports and recommends focused tests for uncovered code paths.
actual_capabilities: Interprets coverage output from Python projects using pytest and coverage tools.
Ranks uncovered lines by risk, including error handling and validation paths.
Suggests specific tests for uncovered functions, branches, and edge cases.
Summarizes module-level coverage gaps and likely impact on coverage goals.
Tracks coverage trends when history data is available in the project.
limitations: Requires current coverage output or project files to produce accurate recommendations.
Does not prove that a test suite catches all defects.
May need project documentation to match local testing conventions.
Package installation or shell commands should require user approval before execution.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Coverage Work Before Release
use_cases.description: Review uncovered files and identify the tests that most improve release confidence.

use_cases.title: Plan Focused Tests For A Feature
use_cases.description: Find uncovered branches in new code and convert them into concrete test scenarios.

use_cases.title: Monitor Coverage Quality Over Time
use_cases.description: Compare recent coverage results and spot regressions before they reach the main branch.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Current Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review after generating a coverage report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the current test coverage report. Summarize overall coverage, uncovered files, and the highest priority gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Find Critical Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for risky untested paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find critical uncovered paths in this project. Prioritize validation, error handling, security checks, and public APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest Tests For One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted planning for a module with low coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest tests for uncovered code in this file. Include test names, scenarios, fixtures, and expected behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Trend-Based Remediation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced coverage planning across multiple reports.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare recent coverage results and create a remediation plan. Separate quick wins, high-risk gaps, and longer-term testing work.

output_examples.input: Analyze coverage after a test run shows 75 percent total coverage.
output: Executive summary with current coverage, target gap, and release risk.
Ranked list of uncovered files and functions that need attention.
Recommended tests that would raise coverage above the project threshold.

output_examples.input: Find critical gaps in a validators module.
output: Identifies untested error handling and invalid input cases.
Explains why each gap matters for production behavior.
Suggests focused unit tests and parametrized cases.

output_examples.input: Review coverage trend data for the last month.
output: Highlights modules where progress has stalled.
Recommends the next coverage tasks by impact and effort.

best_practices: Run coverage with the same command used by the project quality gate.
Prioritize tests for behavior, error handling, and public interfaces before chasing percentages.
Review generated recommendations against project conventions before adding tests.
anti_patterns: Adding shallow tests only to execute lines without checking behavior.
Mocking all dependencies when a real integration path is safe and useful.
Running package installation or shell commands without user approval.

faq.question: What coverage tools does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It is written for Python projects that use pytest, coverage.py, and common make targets.

faq.question: Can it write the tests for me?
faq.answer: It can suggest test names, scenarios, fixtures, and assertions. The final implementation should follow project conventions.

faq.question: Does high coverage mean the code is safe?
faq.answer: No. Coverage shows which code ran during tests. It does not prove that behavior is correct.

faq.question: Should I run every command in the skill?
faq.answer: No. Review commands first, especially package installation and shell commands that write files.

faq.question: Can it analyze coverage trends?
faq.answer: Yes, when the project has prior coverage data or a coverage history file to compare.

faq.question: Is this only for new code?
faq.answer: No. It can analyze new features, legacy modules, and release readiness checks.
